name: Mythology for Sleep
description: Pantheons and epic cycles told as slow, settling stories rather than dramatic action. Each chapter takes one figure, one myth or one long journey from a named tradition and tells it plainly, keeping the culture’s own frame. No battle spectacle, no ranking of gods, no cliffhangers — just the old stories, told until the listener drifts off.
channel_promise: The old stories, told slowly enough to sleep to.
audience: Sleep listeners who love myth and folklore, and anyone who wants the stories told with respect for the tradition rather than as a battle recap.
tagline: The old stories, told until you drift off.
perspective_policy: Third-person storyteller, naming the tradition each story comes from. Never flatten different traditions into one pantheon, and never present myth as documented history.

narrative_quality_contract.opening_policy: Open by naming the tradition and the figure or cycle. No epic framing, no teaser, no promise of a showdown.
required_habits: Name the tradition and the region before the story begins.
Keep violence at a distance; describe consequence rather than spectacle.
Do not rank gods or cultures, and do not merge traditions into one pantheon.
Present myth as myth. Never claim it happened, and never use it as evidence for a real event.
narrative_quality_contract.closing_policy: Let the story settle into its own image — a river, a hall, a long road — with no moralising and no tease for the next episode.

opening_profile.label: Sleep landing
opening_profile.description: A gentle branded welcome and settling ritual before the story begins.

beats.custom_text: a gentle greeting and the channel name, slowly, with no energy in it
name tonight’s tradition and the figure or cycle as things, never as promises or hooks
one gentle question they can answer in the comments before they drift, about a story their family told
one soft line, said now rather than later — after the breathing it would only wake them
lead three slow breaths, paced by the length of the sentences themselves
invite them to close their eyes as the story begins

visual_style_hint: quiet mythic imagery — a river at dusk, a stone hall, a distant figure on a long road; soft and spacious, never a battle scene

metadata_profile.label: Sleep mythology package
metadata_profile.description: A quiet summary naming what the episode explains, a gentle chapter list, and minimal discoverability details; no urgency or sales language.

narrative_rules: Each chapter is one self-contained myth, figure or journey from a named tradition; a listener joining mid-video needs no earlier chapter.
Name the tradition and the region. Never blend Greek, Norse, Egyptian, Mesopotamian, Hindu, Yoruba, Japanese or Khmer material into one pantheon.
Keep violence at a distance: the consequence matters more than the blow.
Present myth as myth, never as documented history or as evidence for a real event.
No ranking of gods, no “the most powerful”, no claim that one tradition is older or truer than another.
title_rules: Name the tradition and the figure or story; calm, literary and specific.
Shapes that work: 'The Long Road of Odysseus', 'Three Egyptian Stories of the Dead', 'What the Norse Gods Feared'.
No all-caps, no question marks, no “epic”, no battle words.

pacing_arc: Chapter 1: the most familiar story, told most simply — it teaches the listener the rhythm of the night.
Chapters 2–{lastButOne}: one myth or figure each, varying tradition and mood between neighbours so the ear travels gently.
Chapter {last}: the quietest story and the softest telling; nothing here should wake them.
additional_rules: Each chapter opens by naming its tradition, region and figure, then tells the story in order without hurry.
Explain an unfamiliar name or practice once, plainly, and then trust the listener.
No per-chapter hook, no “and then everything changed”, no cliffhanger. Close each chapter on a still image.
Write for the ear: long, even sentences, no lists read aloud.
Chapter headings use Arabic numbers only (Chapter 1, Chapter 2…) followed by the story’s plain name.

example_topics: Three Egyptian Stories of the Dead
A Night in the Hall of the Greek Gods
The Slow Journey of the Sun
What the Japanese Gods Left Behind
Khmer Stories of the Neak Ta
Twelve Quiet Stories of the Underworld
audience_hint: Sleep listeners who love myth and folklore, and anyone who wants the stories told with respect for the tradition rather than as a battle recap.
evidence_expectations: Name the tradition and the kind of source (epic, hymn, oral tradition) in plain language.
Where versions differ, say so calmly; never resolve a disagreement by invention.
Never treat a myth as a historical record or as proof of a real event.
idea_system_prompt_role: You generate ideas for a mythology channel made for sleep. Each idea takes one figure, myth or journey from a named tradition and tells it as a slow, settling story. Never a battle recap, never a showdown.
idea_guidance_text: Name the tradition and the story shape; vary tradition and mood across a batch. The point is to settle, not to impress.
script_context: This is a sleep-mythology documentary. Each chapter tells one myth from one named tradition, slowly and in order, for a listener drifting toward sleep. Violence stays at a distance and the story is always presented as myth.
script_system_prompt_role: You are a calm storyteller of myths writing bedtime documentaries. You name the tradition, tell the story in order, keep violence at a distance, and never present myth as history. You never hook, tease, rank gods, or merge traditions.
script_closing_hint: Slow the pace and soften the language as each chapter closes. End on a still image from the story — a river, a hall, a road — with no moralising and no tease.

logline_shape_rules: One calm sentence naming the tradition and the story’s quiet centre.
No stakes, no promise, no question.
theme_shape_rules: Pick 2–4 mythic or atmospheric keywords (fate, river, descent).

metadata_description.voice_guidance: Quiet and plain. List the chapters as a simple timestamped index; no exclamation marks, no sales language.
description_shape_rules: First line: which tradition and which stories tonight, in one calm sentence.
Then a chapter index, one story per line.
Then one gentle line inviting a comment about a story they grew up with.
Close with the calm disclosure and a few hashtags.
metadata_description.cta_shape: One soft line inviting them to keep the video for another night; never “like and subscribe now”.
